title: Recover a weak target residue without resolving its feedback pole
statement: For three calibrated loads0,+r,-r,0<r<1,c=(h_r-h_-r)/(2r),d=(h_r+h_-r-2h0)/(2r) satisfy |d|<=r|c| and Psi=c-d^2/c=a,with Psi(0,0)=0. Explicit radial clipping yields |p_hat-p|<=(1/r+3r+8)epsilon_h,uniformly at zero signal and an unresolved pole.

requires: Same reciprocal source across the three known target loads
Three complex fields with simultaneous error epsilon_h
Explicit feasible radial clip and certified numerical errors
provides: Uniform linear absolute target-power error bound
No separate accurate feedback-pole estimate required
assumptions: The complex feasible set is nonconvex;nearest projection is not assumed nonexpansive
costs: Charge all raw powers,reference/signal photons,combiner loss,calibration,mask writes,load switching,settling and reset;no free parameter,clock or arbitrarily strong local oscillator.
contract.units: Dimensionless power per incident feed-power unit;field amplitude is its square root. r,z,s are complex reflection amplitudes;R is reference amplitude. Physical photon/time calibration remains an acquired input.
contract.obstruction: Does not warrant a common phase,known target-load scale or relative precision of an unresolved signal.
